When we first reported on the federal probe into Los Angeles Dodgers owner Mark Walter over the weekend, many of you jumped into the comments to ask: What sparked the government’s interest? This morning, our reporters map out the web of hidden deals that caught the feds’ attention.

4. READ IT HERE FIRST

 

A web of hidden deals snared the Dodgers owner in a federal probe.

 

Mark Walter stunned the sports world in 2012 with a deal that left his wealthy rivals wondering how the chief executive of Guggenheim Partners, little-known outside Wall Street, had funded the purchase of the Los Angeles Dodgers, one of the premier teams in Major League Baseball. Few moguls can now claim they aren’t familiar with Walter and his international sports kingdom, which included the Los Angeles Lakers. His playbook, using loans from insurance companies he controls to finance his other investments, is now under government scrutiny. Facing pressure from investigators and regulators, the billionaire is racing to unwind bets and save his sports-and-finance empire, report Justin Baer, Margot Patrick, Joe Wallace and Andrew Beaton.

 

5.

 

Here’s how Wall Street sussed out that Situational Awareness was on the ropes.

 

Whispers of strange options trades. A forced sale of Anthropic shares. Banks and traders caught wind that Situational Awareness was in trouble and swung into action. The swift unwind of AI wunderkind Leopold Aschenbrenner’s hedge fund shows how quickly information can spread across Wall Street when a trader is on the ropes—and how fast it can lead to an avalanche of selling. It’s a brutal lesson, too, in the risks of leverage, or investment bets fueled by borrowing, several years after Archegos Capital’s implosion, report Gregory Zuckerman, Juliet Chung and Peter Rudegeair.
